parts.gloss: those who are mad or deluded

words.gloss: even than those who are mad or deluded

literal: Even than those who are mad, a greater fool is he who, being alone, the enmity of many incurs.
translation: One who stands alone and yet incurs the enmity of many is a far greater fool than those who have lost their minds.
modern: துணையின்றித் தனித்து நின்று பலருடைய பகையைத் தேடிக்கொள்பவன், பித்து பிடித்தவர்களை விடவும் அறிவிலி ஆவான்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the extreme foolishness of provoking conflict without having any support. The word 'ēmuṟṟavar' refers to those who are mentally deranged or deluded. The poet asserts that even such madmen are wiser than a person who, standing completely alone ('tamiyaṉāy'), goes out of his way to earn the hostility of many people ('pallār pakai'). Such behavior is not brave but is the height of ignorance, leading to certain ruin.
